MINING ASSOCIATION
DAVID R. COLE, Denver Secretary and Manager
July 10, 1972
The Honorable Rogers C. B. Morton Secretary of the Interior U. S. Department of the Interior Washington, D. C. 20240
Action Office_ For info only
RE: PROPOSED IMPLEMENTATION
EXECUTIVE ORDER 11644
Dear Secretary Morton:
The Colorado Mining Association is the principal organization of individuals and companies engaged in exploration, mining and sales of mineral products in Colorado. Its membership ranges from small miners and prospectors to executives of some of the world's largest mining companies, and encompasses technical talents that are truly representative of today's mining industry. The Colorado Mining Association thus is well qualified to act as spokesman for the industry.
We have reviewed the proposed implementation of E.O.11644, pertaining to the use of off-road vehicles on public land.
The Colorado Mining Association objects to regulations currently under consideration. These regulations would have an adverse effect on prospecting for and mining of minerals on public lands.
A permit system to regulate OEV used in mining would unduly hinder and discourage legitimate mineral exploration, development and mining on public lands.
In most cases ORV use is on existing or established roads.
In many cases ORV needs cannot be anticipated very far in advance of their use. Also, exploration is a very computitive business; permit applications would tend to serve notice of intended exploration activity.
Thank you for the opportunity to bring these views to your attention.
Sincerely yours,
38
COLORADO MINING ASSOCIATION
David R. Cole
Manager
